title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US stocks slid Monday - Dow -0.7% to 51,481.51, S&P 500 -0.8% to 7,683.69, Nasdaq -0.9% to 26,820.38 - as Treasury yields spiked; futures point lower again Tuesday.

Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped to 5.24%, a fresh 19-year high, while Brent crude rose to ~$105/bbl (+0.9%) on Iran/Strait of Hormuz uncertainty; gold fell to ~$4,153 and Bitcoin held near $83.5k.
Companies: Nvidia gained ~1.5%, the lone bright spot in a down market, after unveiling a record $150B stock buyback.
Companies: Boeing sank 6-7% after the WSJ reported a 737 MAX software glitch; the FAA says it won't certify the MAX 10 until the issue is assessed.

Companies: OpenAI paused training on its most capable models after disclosing internal safety/security incidents; Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei held a private White House dinner with Trump as AI leaders' political profile grows.

Macro/Policy: Surging yields and oil are reinforcing a hawkish Fed outlook, with the Iran/Hormuz standoff remaining the dominant macro risk ahead of Tuesday's Case-Shiller, consumer confidence, and JOLTS data.
